title: Atomistic PINN Lab: reproduction of the PINN bond-order potential for aluminum
description:
A research-grade, verification-first reproduction of the physically informed neural network (PINN) bond-order potential for aluminum introduced by Purja Pun, Batra, Ramprasad and Mishin, Nature Communications 10, 2339 (2019). A small neural network maps 60 local descriptors to the eight parameters of an analytical bond-order potential (Eqs. 6-12), keeping extrapolation physics-guided.

The package implements: full-PBC neighbor lists; the 60-dimensional Legendre/Gaussian descriptors (Eqs. 3-5) with proven closed-form identities; the complete BOP physics layer validated against an independent reference transcription (rtol 1e-9) and closed forms; the Eq. (13) objective with a labeled uncertainty ledger for every value the paper leaves unspecified; a Davidson-Fletcher-Powell optimizer with seeded random restarts; provenance-complete checkpoints; evaluation metrics, full-pipeline finite-difference and autograd forces, and 10-fold cross-validation; and an ASE calculator with seeded NVE/NVT molecular-dynamics machinery (energy-drift gate, extrapolation guard).

206 automated tests in three classes (unit / integration / scientific_validation) plus ruff and mypy gates run on every commit. The paper's own DFT database is not publicly available; training results use the public ANI-Al database (Smith et al., Nat. Commun. 12, 92 (2021)) and are reported as a methodological reproduction (alternative data), never as an exact reproduction.

Units: Angstrom, eV, eV/Angstrom throughout. Python 3.11+; CPU-only PyTorch is sufficient.
